title: Named wave in the Waves screen: save the ticked set under a name and launch a saved wave by name
lead: *Proposed.* The Waves screen saves its ticked set under a name and launches a saved wave by name, using the daemon methods and the state file that `named-wave` adds. This slice depends on `named-wave` and cannot start before it has landed.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner, 2026-10-31 (interactive questions on the v1.1 plan): the Waves screen saves its ticked set under a name and launches a saved wave by name; done members show as done and are skipped on start; run records carry the wave name. The state file, the `wave.define`, `wave.list` and `wave.rm` methods, the `name` on `wave.start` and the `wave_name` on the run record are the `named-wave` slice. This slice is only the screen.

Today the owner's ticks and lineup inputs are lost when the screen closes: the ticked set lives in `wavesState.picked` (`internal/tui/waves.go:43`), and `dropWaves` (`:77-82`) discards it. The screen offers `space` tick, `enter` open, `l` launch, `e` edit lineup and `A` show all (`internal/tui/keys.go:411-423`; `docs/dashboard.md`, Waves, ~`:1160-1410`). Launch runs the spec check for every ticked item, then one y/n confirmation showing `ork wave start PROJECT ID...`, then `wave.start` (`confirmWave` `:377-387`, `startWave` `:395-415`).

Why two slices: the screen needs the daemon methods and the shared `Startable` rule, and saving, listing and loading, with their goldens at two sizes, are about a whole M run on their own (`named-wave` is the state, daemon and CLI part).

Open owner questions (MANIFEST-E.md, NW-Q7 to NW-Q9, plus NW-Q1 to NW-Q6 from `named-wave`). Do not start before they are answered; replace each `[NW-Qn]` below with the answer.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
This slice touches no internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd path: it is N-class and can share a wave with an E-class slice that does not edit `internal/tui` or `docs/dashboard.md`. NW-Q9 is answered (no wave name in the TUI), so it stays N-class.

- `internal/tui/waves.go` (saved-wave state in wavesState, the untick and plan-reply queue, startWave sending the name; wavesParts draws the list in place of the table).
- `internal/tui/savedwaves.go` (new): the name input, the saved-wave list view, the load, the refusals of w and L.
- `internal/tui/keys.go` (SaveWave and SavedWaves in keyMap and newKeyMap; the Waves case of contextHints, where the tick hint is now `space tick` and `enter item` drops first, adj 270; the hint cases of the name input and the list).
- `internal/tui/model.go` (key routing for the name input and the list, the w and L cases, paste into the name input), `internal/tui/projects.go` (projectTextEntry) and `internal/tui/view.go` (the name prompt in the status area, the Waves help sentence).
- `internal/tui/live.go` (the Live interface gains WaveDefine and WaveList) and `internal/tui/daemon.go` (the wrappers, beside WaveStart).
- `internal/tui/live_test.go` (fakeLive gains the two methods), `internal/tui/waves_test.go` and `internal/tui/hint_test.go` (the Waves hint assertions follow `space tick` and the dropped `enter item`).
- `testdata/golden/waves-saved-list-*.txt` and `testdata/golden/waves-name-input-*.txt` (new; produced by go test ./internal/tui -update, reviewed by eye), and the existing Waves goldens, whose hint line changes.
- `docs/dashboard.md` (a Saved waves section in Waves; the hint paragraph), `docs/guide.md` (section 9 from :417, and the key table) and `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under ## Unreleased, marked *proposed*).

Pair planning: N-class. It can pair with an E-class slice, and it must come after named-wave. It shares `docs/dashboard.md` and `internal/tui/waves.go` with other Waves slices, so do not pair it with another UI slice that edits those files.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
`internal/tui/waves_test.go` (the new `Live` methods, keys and state do not exist, so these fail to compile first; goldens fail until written). The daemon types are `daemon.WaveDefineParams`, `daemon.SavedWave` and `daemon.SavedWaveView`. NW-Q3 is answered (refuse a duplicate unless replace is set; the screen asks first), so the duplicate case is the replace test and `TestWavesSaveShowsTheDaemonsRefusal` uses `bad_params`.
- `TestWavesSaveNeedsATickedItem`: the save key with nothing ticked shows a status and calls nothing.
- `TestWavesSaveAsksForAName`: with two ticked items (ticked in reverse table order) and a plan for each, the save key opens a one-line name input; `esc` cancels without a call; `enter` calls `WaveDefine` once with the project, the name and the ticked ids in table order.
- `TestWavesSaveShowsTheDaemonsRefusal`: a refused name (`bad_params`) shows the daemon message verbatim in the status line and keeps the input open with the name.
- `TestWavesSaveAsksBeforeReplacingWhenNWQ3AllowsReplace`: a `duplicate_name` reply asks `Replace NAME? [y/N] (Enter is No)`; Enter sends nothing and returns to the name; `y` sends the call again with replace.
- `TestWavesSavedListShowsNamesMembersAndStatus`: the list key calls `WaveList` for the project and shows each saved wave with its members; a done member reads `done`, a missing one `missing`. Also `TestWavesSavedListShowsEmptyAndErrors`, `TestWavesSavedListEnterLoadsTheWaveUnderTheCursor` and `TestWavesSavedListShowsTheMembersOfTheWaveUnderTheCursor` (with more saved waves than the body holds, the members of the wave under the cursor stay on screen).
- `TestWavesLoadTicksTheStartableMembersPresentInTheTable`: choosing a saved wave ticks the members that are startable and are rows of the table, in table order, and plans them one after another (the `space` flow; the tick asks no y/n inputs since adj 189); done members are not ticked and are named in the status line. Also `TestWavesLoadShowsAMemberInAHiddenWave` and `TestWavesLoadNeverLaunches`.
- `TestWavesLoadNamesMembersNotInTheSuggestion`: a startable member that is not a row of the table (blocked, held, unspecified in the plan) is named with its reason and is not ticked.
- `TestWavesLaunchAfterLoadSendsTheWaveName`: `l` then `y` sends `WaveStartParams.Name` equal to the loaded name when the launched items are exactly the startable members; after the owner unticks one, adds one, or a member is not in the table, or for a hand-ticked set, no name is sent.
- `TestWavesSavedKeysDoNothingOnTheAggregateTab`: the combined Running-entry tab is read-only (S140) and stays so; the keys work on a project tab first.
- `TestWavesSavedKeysAreHiddenWithoutADaemon`: with no `Live`, the keys are refused and absent from the hint. Also `TestWavesSavedKeysAreRefusedWhileAPlanOrStartIsInFlight`.
- `TestWavesHintLinesShowSaveAndSavedAt100And80Columns` (owner, adj 270, ui.waves-hint-priority): `L saved` shows with nothing ticked; the tick hint is `space tick` and, with two ticked, `enter item` goes first, so `space tick; l launch; e edit lineup; w save; L saved; q quit; ? help` fits at 100x30, `L saved` goes next at 80x24, and `enter item` shows again at 120; the name input hint. Also `TestWavesHelpListsTheSavedWaveKeys` (the keys ride on the Waves help sentence and cost the help no line) and `TestDaemonAdapterSavesAndListsWaves`. The existing hint assertions in `internal/tui/hint_test.go` and `waves_test.go` follow `space tick`.
- Goldens (`golden_test.go` helpers): `waves-saved-list-100x30-{color,mono}.txt`, `waves-saved-list-80x24-{color,mono}.txt` with the `-ascii` variants, and `waves-name-input-100x30-mono.txt`, `waves-name-input-80x24-mono.txt`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first. Do not touch: `internal/daemon`, `internal/engine`, `internal/cli`, the `wavestore` package (all `named-wave`), the spec-check sitting, the lineup editor, or the aggregate Waves tab's read-only rule.

1. Preflight: `named-wave` has landed and its methods exist (`rg -n "MethodWaveDefine" internal/daemon/wire.go`). The owner has answered NW-Q7 to NW-Q9 and NW-Q1 to NW-Q6. If not, stop and report.
2. `Live`: add `WaveDefine(ctx, daemon.DefineWaveParams) (*daemon.SavedWave, error)` and `WaveList(ctx, project string) ([]daemon.SavedWaveView, error)`; wrappers in `internal/tui/daemon.go` open a connection per call, as `WaveStart` does (`:169-177`). Update `fakeLive` and every other type that embeds it.
3. Keys: the save key and the saved-list key per `[NW-Q7]`. Offer them in the Waves hint only when a daemon is connected, the tab is not the aggregate tab, the plan has loaded, and (for save) at least one item is ticked with a plan (the same guards as `tickRefusal` and `waveLaunchRefusal`, `:242-262` and `:348-375`). Both keys are refused while a spec check, a plan or a start is in flight.
4. Save: one-line name input in the action area (reuse the `textField` the inputs use). `enter` sends `WaveDefine`. The result sets a status line `saved NAME: A, B`. Ticks stay.
5. Saved list: replaces the table body while open, like the item pane. One block per wave: `NAME` then one row per member with its id, status and title. Keys: `up/down` move, `enter` loads the wave under the cursor, `esc` returns. Removing a saved wave stays CLI-only (`ork wave rm`); say so in the hint-free help text of `docs/dashboard.md`.
6. Load: per `[NW-Q8]`. The default in the tests above: tick the startable members that are rows of the table, queue their y/n inputs one after another (the existing `tickWave` flow), and send the name on launch only when the launched set equals the startable set. Done members stay unticked and are named in the status line. A load never launches by itself: the owner presses `l`, so the spec check, the overlap warnings, the engine-conflict mark and the confirmation all run as for a hand-ticked set.
7. Wave name in the run pane: only if `[NW-Q9]` says so (see the manifest); the default is not to show it.
8. Docs: `docs/dashboard.md` (the keys, the saved list, a sample at 80x24, the load rules, *proposed* markers), `docs/guide.md` section 9. Rewrite the goldens with `go test ./internal/tui -update` and review every diff by eye; no existing golden may change except the Waves hint line if the hint is part of it.
9. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`, starting `Named wave in the Waves screen (*proposed*):`.

UI slice: UI pass (r14).

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). NW-Q1 to NW-Q9 are answered as drafted; see S215's Owner decisions paragraph (no wave name in the TUI for now, so this slice's TUI save and load needs the owner to confirm its scope before it starts).

Owner decisions (2026-11-10): Does the owner confirm S216's TUI save and load scope, now that NW-Q9 is "no wave name in the TUI"? -> confirm as written: build the screen as the spec says. `w` saves the ticked set, `L` lists and loads saved waves (NW-Q7). Load ticks the startable members that are table rows and names the rest (NW-Q8 a). `l` sends `WaveStartParams.Name` only when the launched set equals the startable set. The name is not shown in the TUI (NW-Q9 a)..

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/tui`.
- `git diff --stat -- testdata/golden` lists only the new `waves-saved-*` and `waves-name-*` files and, if the hint changed, the existing Waves goldens.
- [HUMAN CHECK] At 100x30 and 80x24 in a live terminal: tick two items, save under a name, close and reopen Waves, open the saved list, load the wave, and confirm the ticks, the done member, and the status text read clearly and nothing wraps badly.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] Launch a saved wave from the screen once with a real pair of small slices, then check the run record carries `wave_name` (`ork status --json`).
